[884](#884)
[885](#885)    fn eliminate_cse(&mut self, instructions: &mut [Instruction]) -> OptResult {
[887](#887)        let mut expr_map: HashMap<ExprKey, Reg> = HashMap::new();
[889](#889)
[890](#890)        let mut reg_map: HashMap<Reg, Reg> = HashMap::new();
[892](#892)
[893](#893)        let mut modified = 0;
[894](#894)
[895](#895)        for inst in instructions.iter_mut() {
[896](#896)            if inst.is_dead {
[897](#897)                continue;
[898](#898)            }
[899](#899)
[900](#900)            let opcode = inst.opcode.clone();
[902](#902)
[903](#903)            let resolve = |r: Reg| -> Reg { reg_map.get(&r).copied().unwrap_or(r) };
[905](#905)
[906](#906)            let dests_to_invalidate: Vec<Reg> = match &opcode {
[927](#927)                Opcode::Add { dest, .. }
[928](#928)                | Opcode::Sub { dest, .. }
[929](#929)                | Opcode::Mul { dest, .. }
[930](#930)                | Opcode::DivS { dest, .. }
[931](#931)                | Opcode::DivU { dest, .. }
[932](#932)                | Opcode::RemS { dest, .. }
[933](#933)                | Opcode::RemU { dest, .. }
[934](#934)                | Opcode::And { dest, .. }
[935](#935)                | Opcode::Or { dest, .. }
[936](#936)                | Opcode::Xor { dest, .. }
[937](#937)                | Opcode::Shl { dest, .. }
[938](#938)                | Opcode::ShrS { dest, .. }
[939](#939)                | Opcode::ShrU { dest, .. }
[940](#940)                | Opcode::Rotl { dest, .. }
[941](#941)                | Opcode::Rotr { dest, .. }
[942](#942)                | Opcode::Clz { dest, .. }
[943](#943)                | Opcode::Ctz { dest, .. }
[944](#944)                | Opcode::Popcnt { dest, .. }
[945](#945)                | Opcode::Extend8S { dest, .. }
[946](#946)                | Opcode::Extend16S { dest, .. }
[947](#947)                | Opcode::Eqz { dest, .. }
[948](#948)                | Opcode::Eq { dest, .. }
[949](#949)                | Opcode::Ne { dest, .. }
[950](#950)                | Opcode::LtS { dest, .. }
[951](#951)                | Opcode::LtU { dest, .. }
[952](#952)                | Opcode::LeS { dest, .. }
[953](#953)                | Opcode::LeU { dest, .. }
[954](#954)                | Opcode::GtS { dest, .. }
[955](#955)                | Opcode::GtU { dest, .. }
[956](#956)                | Opcode::GeS { dest, .. }
[957](#957)                | Opcode::GeU { dest, .. }
[958](#958)                | Opcode::Load { dest, .. }
[959](#959)                | Opcode::MemLoad { dest, .. }
[960](#960)                | Opcode::Copy { dest, .. }
[961](#961)                | Opcode::TeeStore { dest, .. }
[962](#962)                | Opcode::Select { dest, .. }
[963](#963)                | Opcode::Const { dest, .. }
[964](#964)                | Opcode::I64Eq { dest, .. }
[965](#965)                | Opcode::I64Ne { dest, .. }
[966](#966)                | Opcode::I64LtS { dest, .. }
[967](#967)                | Opcode::I64LtU { dest, .. }
[968](#968)                | Opcode::I64LeS { dest, .. }
[969](#969)                | Opcode::I64LeU { dest, .. }
[970](#970)                | Opcode::I64GtS { dest, .. }
[971](#971)                | Opcode::I64GtU { dest, .. }
[972](#972)                | Opcode::I64GeS { dest, .. }
[973](#973)                | Opcode::I64GeU { dest, .. }
[974](#974)                | Opcode::I64Eqz { dest, .. }
[975](#975)                | Opcode::I64Clz { dest, .. }
[976](#976)                | Opcode::I64Ctz { dest, .. }
[977](#977)                | Opcode::I64Popcnt { dest, .. }
[978](#978)                | Opcode::I32WrapI64 { dest, .. }
[979](#979)                | Opcode::MemLoadSubword { dest, .. }
[980](#980)                | Opcode::GlobalGet { dest, .. }
[981](#981)                | Opcode::MemorySize { dest, .. }
[982](#982)                | Opcode::MemoryGrow { dest, .. }
[983](#983)                | Opcode::Call { dest, .. } => vec![*dest],
[984](#984)                Opcode::I64Add {
[985](#985)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[986](#986)                }
[987](#987)                | Opcode::I64Sub {
[988](#988)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[989](#989)                }
[990](#990)                | Opcode::I64And {
[991](#991)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[992](#992)                }
[993](#993)                | Opcode::I64Or {
[994](#994)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[995](#995)                }
[996](#996)                | Opcode::I64Xor {
[997](#997)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[998](#998)                }
[999](#999)                | Opcode::I64Mul {
[1000](#1000)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1001](#1001)                }
[1002](#1002)                | Opcode::I64DivS {
[1003](#1003)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1004](#1004)                }
[1005](#1005)                | Opcode::I64DivU {
[1006](#1006)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1007](#1007)                }
[1008](#1008)                | Opcode::I64RemS {
[1009](#1009)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1010](#1010)                }
[1011](#1011)                | Opcode::I64RemU {
[1012](#1012)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1013](#1013)                }
[1014](#1014)                | Opcode::I64Shl {
[1015](#1015)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1016](#1016)                }
[1017](#1017)                | Opcode::I64ShrS {
[1018](#1018)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1019](#1019)                }
[1020](#1020)                | Opcode::I64ShrU {
[1021](#1021)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1022](#1022)                }
[1023](#1023)                | Opcode::I64Rotl {
[1024](#1024)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1025](#1025)                }
[1026](#1026)                | Opcode::I64Rotr {
[1027](#1027)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1028](#1028)                }
[1029](#1029)                | Opcode::I64Const {
[1030](#1030)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1031](#1031)                }
[1032](#1032)                | Opcode::I64Load {
[1033](#1033)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1034](#1034)                }
[1035](#1035)                | Opcode::I64Extend8S {
[1036](#1036)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1037](#1037)                }
[1038](#1038)                | Opcode::I64Extend16S {
[1039](#1039)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1040](#1040)                }
[1041](#1041)                | Opcode::I64Extend32S {
[1042](#1042)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1043](#1043)                }
[1044](#1044)                | Opcode::I64ExtendI32U {
[1045](#1045)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1046](#1046)                }
[1047](#1047)                | Opcode::I64ExtendI32S {
[1048](#1048)                    dest_lo, dest_hi, ..
[1049](#1049)                } => vec![*dest_lo, *dest_hi],
[1050](#1050)                _ => Vec::new(),
[1051](#1051)            };
[1052](#1052)
[1053](#1053)            match opcode {
[1054](#1054)                Opcode::Add { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[1055](#1055)                    let src1 = resolve(src1);
[1056](#1056)                    let src2 = resolve(src2);
[1057](#1057)                    let key = ExprKey::Add(src1, src2);
[1058](#1058)
[1059](#1059)                    if let Some(&existing) = expr_map.get(&key) {
[1060](#1060)                        inst.opcode = Opcode::Const { dest, value: 0 }; inst.is_dead = true; reg_map.insert(dest, existing);
[1064](#1064)                        modified += 1;
[1065](#1065)
[1066](#1066)                        if self.verbose {
[1067](#1067)                            eprintln!(
[1068](#1068)                                "CSE: Eliminated add r{} = r{} + r{}, reuse r{}",
[1069](#1069)                                dest.0, src1.0, src2.0, existing.0
[1070](#1070)                            );
[1071](#1071)                        }
[1072](#1072)                    } else {
[1073](#1073)                        expr_map.insert(key, dest);
[1074](#1074)                        inst.opcode = Opcode::Add { dest, src1, src2 };
[1076](#1076)                    }
[1077](#1077)                }
[1078](#1078)
[1079](#1079)                Opcode::Sub { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[1080](#1080)                    let src1 = resolve(src1);
[1081](#1081)                    let src2 = resolve(src2);
[1082](#1082)                    let key = ExprKey::Sub(src1, src2);
[1083](#1083)
[1084](#1084)                    if let Some(&existing) = expr_map.get(&key) {
[1085](#1085)                        inst.opcode = Opcode::Const { dest, value: 0 };
[1086](#1086)                        inst.is_dead = true;
[1087](#1087)                        reg_map.insert(dest, existing);
[1088](#1088)                        modified += 1;
[1089](#1089)
[1090](#1090)                        if self.verbose {
[1091](#1091)                            eprintln!(
[1092](#1092)                                "CSE: Eliminated sub r{} = r{} - r{}, reuse r{}",
[1093](#1093)                                dest.0, src1.0, src2.0, existing.0
[1094](#1094)                            );
[1095](#1095)                        }
[1096](#1096)                    } else {
[1097](#1097)                        expr_map.insert(key, dest);
[1098](#1098)                        inst.opcode = Opcode::Sub { dest, src1, src2 };
[1099](#1099)                    }
[1100](#1100)                }
[1101](#1101)
[1102](#1102)                Opcode::Mul { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[1103](#1103)                    let src1 = resolve(src1);
[1104](#1104)                    let src2 = resolve(src2);
[1105](#1105)                    let key = ExprKey::Mul(src1, src2);
[1106](#1106)
[1107](#1107)                    if let Some(&existing) = expr_map.get(&key) {
[1108](#1108)                        inst.opcode = Opcode::Const { dest, value: 0 };
[1109](#1109)                        inst.is_dead = true;
[1110](#1110)                        reg_map.insert(dest, existing);
[1111](#1111)                        modified += 1;
[1112](#1112)
[1113](#1113)                        if self.verbose {
[1114](#1114)                            eprintln!(
[1115](#1115)                                "CSE: Eliminated mul r{} = r{} * r{}, reuse r{}",
[1116](#1116)                                dest.0, src1.0, src2.0, existing.0
[1117](#1117)                            );
[1118](#1118)                        }
[1119](#1119)                    } else {
[1120](#1120)                        expr_map.insert(key, dest);
[1121](#1121)                        inst.opcode = Opcode::Mul { dest, src1, src2 };
[1122](#1122)                    }
[1123](#1123)                }
[1124](#1124)
[1125](#1125)                Opcode::Load { dest, addr } => {
[1126](#1126)                    let key = ExprKey::Load(addr);
[1127](#1127)
[1128](#1128)                    if let Some(&existing) = expr_map.get(&key) {
[1129](#1129)                        inst.opcode = Opcode::Const { dest, value: 0 };
[1130](#1130)                        inst.is_dead = true;
[1131](#1131)                        reg_map.insert(dest, existing);
[1132](#1132)                        modified += 1;
[1133](#1133)
[1134](#1134)                        if self.verbose {
[1135](#1135)                            eprintln!(
[1136](#1136)                                "CSE: Eliminated load r{} = [0x{:x}], reuse r{}",
[1137](#1137)                                dest.0, addr, existing.0
[1138](#1138)                            );
[1139](#1139)                        }
[1140](#1140)                    } else {
[1141](#1141)                        expr_map.insert(key, dest);
[1142](#1142)                    }
[1143](#1143)                }
[1144](#1144)
[1145](#1145)                Opcode::Store { src, addr } => {
[1149](#1149)                    let src = resolve(src);
[1150](#1150)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::Store { src, addr };
[1151](#1151)                    expr_map.remove(&ExprKey::Load(addr));
[1152](#1152)                }
[1153](#1153)
[1154](#1154)                Opcode::TeeStore { dest, src, addr } => {
[1157](#1157)                    let src = resolve(src);
[1158](#1158)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::TeeStore { dest, src, addr };
[1159](#1159)                    expr_map.remove(&ExprKey::Load(addr));
[1160](#1160)                }
[1161](#1161)
[1162](#1162)                Opcode::MemLoad { dest, addr, offset } => {
[1176](#1176)                    let addr = resolve(addr);
[1177](#1177)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::MemLoad { dest, addr, offset };
[1178](#1178)                }
[1179](#1179)
[1180](#1180)                Opcode::MemStore { src, addr, offset } => {
[1183](#1183)                    let src = resolve(src);
[1184](#1184)                    let addr = resolve(addr);
[1185](#1185)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::MemStore { src, addr, offset };
[1186](#1186)                }
[1187](#1187)
[1188](#1188)                Opcode::Extend8S { dest, src } => {
[1190](#1190)                    let src = resolve(src);
[1191](#1191)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::Extend8S { dest, src };
[1192](#1192)                }
[1193](#1193)                Opcode::Extend16S { dest, src } => {
[1194](#1194)                    let src = resolve(src);
[1195](#1195)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::Extend16S { dest, src };
[1196](#1196)                }
[1197](#1197)
[1198](#1198)                Opcode::Label { .. } => {
[1201](#1201)                    expr_map.retain(|k, _| !matches!(k, ExprKey::Load(_)));
[1202](#1202)                }
[1203](#1203)
[1204](#1204)                Opcode::CondBranch { cond, target } => {
[1206](#1206)                    let cond = resolve(cond);
[1207](#1207)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::CondBranch { cond, target };
[1208](#1208)                    expr_map.retain(|k, _| !matches!(k, ExprKey::Load(_)));
[1210](#1210)                }
[1211](#1211)
[1212](#1212)                Opcode::Eq { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[1214](#1214)                    let src1 = resolve(src1);
[1215](#1215)                    let src2 = resolve(src2);
[1216](#1216)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::Eq { dest, src1, src2 };
[1217](#1217)                }
[1218](#1218)                Opcode::Ne { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[1219](#1219)                    let src1 = resolve(src1);
[1220](#1220)                    let src2 = resolve(src2);
[1221](#1221)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::Ne { dest, src1, src2 };
[1222](#1222)                }
[1223](#1223)                Opcode::LtS { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[1224](#1224)                    let src1 = resolve(src1);
[1225](#1225)                    let src2 = resolve(src2);
[1226](#1226)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::LtS { dest, src1, src2 };
[1227](#1227)                }
[1228](#1228)                Opcode::LtU { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[1229](#1229)                    let src1 = resolve(src1);
[1230](#1230)                    let src2 = resolve(src2);
[1231](#1231)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::LtU { dest, src1, src2 };
[1232](#1232)                }
[1233](#1233)                Opcode::LeS { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[1234](#1234)                    let src1 = resolve(src1);
[1235](#1235)                    let src2 = resolve(src2);
[1236](#1236)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::LeS { dest, src1, src2 };
[1237](#1237)                }
[1238](#1238)                Opcode::LeU { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[1239](#1239)                    let src1 = resolve(src1);
[1240](#1240)                    let src2 = resolve(src2);
[1241](#1241)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::LeU { dest, src1, src2 };
[1242](#1242)                }
[1243](#1243)                Opcode::GtS { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[1244](#1244)                    let src1 = resolve(src1);
[1245](#1245)                    let src2 = resolve(src2);
[1246](#1246)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::GtS { dest, src1, src2 };
[1247](#1247)                }
[1248](#1248)                Opcode::GtU { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[1249](#1249)                    let src1 = resolve(src1);
[1250](#1250)                    let src2 = resolve(src2);
[1251](#1251)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::GtU { dest, src1, src2 };
[1252](#1252)                }
[1253](#1253)                Opcode::GeS { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[1254](#1254)                    let src1 = resolve(src1);
[1255](#1255)                    let src2 = resolve(src2);
[1256](#1256)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::GeS { dest, src1, src2 };
[1257](#1257)                }
[1258](#1258)                Opcode::GeU { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[1259](#1259)                    let src1 = resolve(src1);
[1260](#1260)                    let src2 = resolve(src2);
[1261](#1261)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::GeU { dest, src1, src2 };
[1262](#1262)                }
[1263](#1263)
[1264](#1264)                Opcode::Eqz { dest, src } => {
[1266](#1266)                    let src = resolve(src);
[1267](#1267)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::Eqz { dest, src };
[1268](#1268)                }
[1269](#1269)
[1270](#1270)                Opcode::Return { value: Some(v) } => {
[1271](#1271)                    let v = resolve(v);
[1272](#1272)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::Return { value: Some(v) };
[1273](#1273)                }
[1274](#1274)

[1950](#1950)                    };
[1951](#1951)                }
[1952](#1952)                Opcode::MemoryGrow { dest, delta } => {
[1953](#1953)                    inst.opcode = Opcode::MemoryGrow {
[1954](#1954)                        dest,
[1955](#1955)                        delta: resolve(delta),
[1956](#1956)                    };
[1957](#1957)                }
[1958](#1958)
[1959](#1959)                _ => {}
[1960](#1960)            }
[1961](#1961)
[1962](#1962)            if !inst.is_dead {
[1969](#1969)                for dest in &dests_to_invalidate {
[1970](#1970)                    reg_map.remove(dest);
[1971](#1971)                }
[1972](#1972)            }
[1973](#1973)        }
[1974](#1974)
[1975](#1975)        if self.verbose && modified > 0 {
[1976](#1976)            eprintln!("CSE: {} subexpressions eliminated", modified);
[1977](#1977)        }
[1978](#1978)
[1979](#1979)        OptResult {
[1980](#1980)            changed: modified > 0,
[1981](#1981)            removed_count: modified, added_count: 0,
[1983](#1983)            modified_count: 0,
[1984](#1984)        }
[1985](#1985)    }

[2004](#2004)pub struct AlgebraicSimplification {
[2006](#2006)    verbose: bool,
[2007](#2007)}
[2008](#2008)
[2009](#2009)impl AlgebraicSimplification {
[2010](#2010)    pub fn new() -> Self {
[2011](#2011)        Self { verbose: false }
[2012](#2012)    }
[2013](#2013)
[2014](#2014)    pub fn with_verbose(mut self) -> Self {
[2015](#2015)        self.verbose = true;
[2016](#2016)        self
[2017](#2017)    }
[2018](#2018)
[2019](#2019)    fn simplify(&mut self, instructions: &mut [Instruction]) -> OptResult {
[2021](#2021)        let mut const_values: HashMap<Reg, i32> = HashMap::new();
[2023](#2023)        let mut modified = 0;
[2024](#2024)
[2025](#2025)        for inst in instructions.iter_mut() {
[2026](#2026)            if inst.is_dead {
[2027](#2027)                continue;
[2028](#2028)            }
[2029](#2029)
[2030](#2030)            let opcode = inst.opcode.clone();
[2031](#2031)
[2032](#2032)            match opcode {
[2033](#2033)                Opcode::Const { dest, value } => {
[2035](#2035)                    const_values.insert(dest, value);
[2036](#2036)                }
[2037](#2037)
[2038](#2038)                Opcode::Add {
[2040](#2040)                    dest: _,
[2041](#2041)                    src1,
[2042](#2042)                    src2,
[2043](#2043)                } => {
[2044](#2044)                    let val1 = const_values.get(&src1);
[2045](#2045)                    let val2 = const_values.get(&src2);
[2046](#2046)
[2047](#2047)                    match (val1, val2) {
[2048](#2048)                        (Some(&0), _) => {
[2049](#2049)                            inst.is_dead = true;
[2051](#2051)                            modified += 1;
[2052](#2052)                            if self.verbose {
[2053](#2053)                                eprintln!("Simplified: 0 + r{} -> r{}", src2.0, src2.0);
[2054](#2054)                            }
[2055](#2055)                        }
[2056](#2056)                        (_, Some(&0)) => {
[2057](#2057)                            inst.is_dead = true;
[2059](#2059)                            modified += 1;
[2060](#2060)                            if self.verbose {
[2061](#2061)                                eprintln!("Simplified: r{} + 0 -> r{}", src1.0, src1.0);
[2062](#2062)                            }
[2063](#2063)                        }
[2064](#2064)                        _ => {}
[2065](#2065)                    }
[2066](#2066)                }
[2067](#2067)
[2068](#2068)                Opcode::Sub { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[2070](#2070)                    let val2 = const_values.get(&src2);
[2071](#2071)
[2072](#2072)                    if let Some(&0) = val2 {
[2073](#2073)                        inst.is_dead = true;
[2075](#2075)                        modified += 1;
[2076](#2076)                        if self.verbose {
[2077](#2077)                            eprintln!("Simplified: r{} - 0 -> r{}", src1.0, src1.0);
[2078](#2078)                        }
[2079](#2079)                    } else if src1 == src2 {
[2080](#2080)                        inst.opcode = Opcode::Const { dest, value: 0 };
[2082](#2082)                        const_values.insert(dest, 0);
[2083](#2083)                        modified += 1;
[2084](#2084)                        if self.verbose {
[2085](#2085)                            eprintln!("Simplified: r{} - r{} -> 0", src1.0, src2.0);
[2086](#2086)                        }
[2087](#2087)                    }
[2088](#2088)                }
[2089](#2089)
[2090](#2090)                Opcode::Mul { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[2092](#2092)                    let val1 = const_values.get(&src1);
[2093](#2093)                    let val2 = const_values.get(&src2);
[2094](#2094)
[2095](#2095)                    match (val1, val2) {
[2096](#2096)                        (Some(&0), _) | (_, Some(&0)) => {
[2097](#2097)                            inst.opcode = Opcode::Const { dest, value: 0 };
[2099](#2099)                            const_values.insert(dest, 0);
[2100](#2100)                            modified += 1;
[2101](#2101)                            if self.verbose {
[2102](#2102)                                eprintln!("Simplified: mul with 0 -> 0");
[2103](#2103)                            }
[2104](#2104)                        }
[2105](#2105)                        (Some(&1), _) => {
[2106](#2106)                            inst.is_dead = true;
[2108](#2108)                            modified += 1;
[2109](#2109)                            if self.verbose {
[2110](#2110)                                eprintln!("Simplified: 1 * r{} -> r{}", src2.0, src2.0);
[2111](#2111)                            }
[2112](#2112)                        }
[2113](#2113)                        (_, Some(&1)) => {
[2114](#2114)                            inst.is_dead = true;
[2116](#2116)                            modified += 1;
[2117](#2117)                            if self.verbose {
[2118](#2118)                                eprintln!("Simplified: r{} * 1 -> r{}", src1.0, src1.0);
[2119](#2119)                            }
[2120](#2120)                        }
[2121](#2121)                        _ => {}
[2122](#2122)                    }
[2123](#2123)                }
[2124](#2124)
[2125](#2125)                _ => {}
[2126](#2126)            }
[2127](#2127)        }
[2128](#2128)
[2129](#2129)        if self.verbose && modified > 0 {
[2130](#2130)            eprintln!(
[2131](#2131)                "Algebraic simplification: {} operations simplified",
[2132](#2132)                modified
[2133](#2133)            );
[2134](#2134)        }
[2135](#2135)
[2136](#2136)        OptResult {
[2137](#2137)            changed: modified > 0,
[2138](#2138)            removed_count: 0,
[2139](#2139)            added_count: 0,
[2140](#2140)            modified_count: modified,
[2141](#2141)        }
[2142](#2142)    }
[2143](#2143)}
[2144](#2144)
[2145](#2145)impl Default for AlgebraicSimplification {
[2146](#2146)    fn default() -> Self {
[2147](#2147)        Self::new()
[2148](#2148)    }
[2149](#2149)}

[2151](#2151)impl OptimizationPass for AlgebraicSimplification {

[2154](#2154)    }

[2156](#2156)    fn run(&mut self, _cfg: &mut Cfg, instructions: &mut Vec<Instruction>) -> OptResult {
[2157](#2157)        self.simplify(instructions)

[2161](#2161)pub struct PeepholeOptimization {
[2163](#2163)    verbose: bool,
[2164](#2164)}
[2165](#2165)
[2166](#2166)impl PeepholeOptimization {
[2167](#2167)    pub fn new() -> Self {
[2168](#2168)        Self { verbose: false }
[2169](#2169)    }
[2170](#2170)
[2171](#2171)    pub fn with_verbose(mut self) -> Self {
[2172](#2172)        self.verbose = true;
[2173](#2173)        self
[2174](#2174)    }
[2175](#2175)
[2176](#2176)    fn optimize(&mut self, instructions: &mut [Instruction]) -> OptResult {
[2178](#2178)        let mut modified = 0;
[2179](#2179)
[2180](#2180)        let mut i = 0;
[2182](#2182)        while i + 1 < instructions.len() {
[2183](#2183)            if instructions[i].is_dead || instructions[i + 1].is_dead {
[2184](#2184)                i += 1;
[2185](#2185)                continue;
[2186](#2186)            }
[2187](#2187)
[2188](#2188)            let inst1 = instructions[i].opcode.clone();
[2189](#2189)            let inst2 = instructions[i + 1].opcode.clone();
[2190](#2190)
[2191](#2191)            match (&inst1, &inst2) {
[2193](#2193)                (Opcode::Const { dest: dest1, .. }, Opcode::Const { dest: dest2, .. })
[2194](#2194)                    if dest1 == dest2 =>
[2195](#2195)                {
[2196](#2196)                    instructions[i].is_dead = true;
[2198](#2198)                    modified += 1;
[2199](#2199)
[2200](#2200)                    if self.verbose {
[2201](#2201)                        eprintln!("Peephole: Eliminated redundant const to r{}", dest1.0);
[2202](#2202)                    }
[2203](#2203)                }
[2204](#2204)
[2205](#2205)                _ => {}
[2207](#2207)            }
[2208](#2208)
[2209](#2209)            i += 1;
[2210](#2210)        }
[2211](#2211)
[2212](#2212)        let mut i = 0;
[2214](#2214)        while i + 2 < instructions.len() {
[2215](#2215)            if instructions[i].is_dead || instructions[i + 1].is_dead || instructions[i + 2].is_dead
[2216](#2216)            {
[2217](#2217)                i += 1;
[2218](#2218)                continue;
[2219](#2219)            }
[2220](#2220)
[2221](#2221)            let _inst1 = instructions[i].opcode.clone();
[2222](#2222)            let _inst2 = instructions[i + 1].opcode.clone();
[2223](#2223)            let _inst3 = instructions[i + 2].opcode.clone();
[2224](#2224)
[2225](#2225)            i += 1;
[2229](#2229)        }
[2230](#2230)
[2231](#2231)        if self.verbose && modified > 0 {
[2232](#2232)            eprintln!("Peephole optimization: {} patterns matched", modified);
[2233](#2233)        }
[2234](#2234)
[2235](#2235)        OptResult {
[2236](#2236)            changed: modified > 0,
[2237](#2237)            removed_count: modified,
[2238](#2238)            added_count: 0,
[2239](#2239)            modified_count: 0,
[2240](#2240)        }
[2241](#2241)    }
[2242](#2242)}
[2243](#2243)
[2244](#2244)impl Default for PeepholeOptimization {
[2245](#2245)    fn default() -> Self {
[2246](#2246)        Self::new()
[2247](#2247)    }
[2248](#2248)}
[2249](#2249)
[2250](#2250)impl OptimizationPass for PeepholeOptimization {
[2251](#2251)    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
[2252](#2252)        "peephole-optimization"
[2253](#2253)    }
[2254](#2254)
[2255](#2255)    fn run(&mut self, _cfg: &mut Cfg, instructions: &mut Vec<Instruction>) -> OptResult {
[2256](#2256)        self.optimize(instructions)

[2260](#2260)pub struct StrengthReduction {
[2262](#2262)    verbose: bool,
[2263](#2263)}
[2264](#2264)
[2265](#2265)impl StrengthReduction {
[2266](#2266)    pub fn new() -> Self {
[2267](#2267)        Self { verbose: false }
[2268](#2268)    }
[2269](#2269)
[2270](#2270)    pub fn with_verbose(mut self) -> Self {
[2271](#2271)        self.verbose = true;
[2272](#2272)        self
[2273](#2273)    }
[2274](#2274)
[2275](#2275)    fn is_power_of_2(n: i32) -> bool {
[2277](#2277)        n > 0 && (n & (n - 1)) == 0
[2278](#2278)    }
[2279](#2279)
[2280](#2280)    fn log2(n: i32) -> u32 {
[2282](#2282)        n.trailing_zeros()
[2283](#2283)    }
[2284](#2284)
[2285](#2285)    fn reduce(&mut self, instructions: &mut [Instruction]) -> OptResult {
[2287](#2287)        let mut const_values: HashMap<Reg, i32> = HashMap::new();
[2288](#2288)        let mut modified = 0;
[2289](#2289)
[2290](#2290)        for inst in instructions.iter_mut() {
[2291](#2291)            if inst.is_dead {
[2292](#2292)                continue;
[2293](#2293)            }
[2294](#2294)
[2295](#2295)            let opcode = inst.opcode.clone();
[2296](#2296)
[2297](#2297)            match opcode {
[2298](#2298)                Opcode::Const { dest, value } => {
[2300](#2300)                    const_values.insert(dest, value);
[2301](#2301)                }
[2302](#2302)
[2303](#2303)                Opcode::Mul {
[2305](#2305)                    dest: _,
[2306](#2306)                    src1,
[2307](#2307)                    src2,
[2308](#2308)                } => {
[2309](#2309)                    let val1 = const_values.get(&src1);
[2310](#2310)                    let val2 = const_values.get(&src2);
[2311](#2311)
[2312](#2312)                    if let Some(&val) = val2
[2313](#2313)                        && Self::is_power_of_2(val)
[2314](#2314)                    {
[2315](#2315)                        modified += 1;
[2318](#2318)                        if self.verbose {
[2319](#2319)                            eprintln!(
[2320](#2320)                                "Strength reduction: r{} * {} -> r{} << {}",
[2321](#2321)                                src1.0,
[2322](#2322)                                val,
[2323](#2323)                                src1.0,
[2324](#2324)                                Self::log2(val)
[2325](#2325)                            );
[2326](#2326)                        }
[2327](#2327)                    } else if let Some(&val) = val1
[2328](#2328)                        && Self::is_power_of_2(val)
[2329](#2329)                    {
[2330](#2330)                        modified += 1;
[2331](#2331)                        if self.verbose {
[2332](#2332)                            eprintln!(
[2333](#2333)                                "Strength reduction: {} * r{} -> r{} << {}",
[2334](#2334)                                val,
[2335](#2335)                                src2.0,
[2336](#2336)                                src2.0,
[2337](#2337)                                Self::log2(val)
[2338](#2338)                            );
[2339](#2339)                        }
[2340](#2340)                    }
[2341](#2341)                }
[2342](#2342)
[2343](#2343)                _ => {}
[2344](#2344)            }
[2345](#2345)        }
[2346](#2346)
[2347](#2347)        if self.verbose && modified > 0 {
[2348](#2348)            eprintln!("Strength reduction: {} operations reduced", modified);
[2349](#2349)        }
[2350](#2350)
[2351](#2351)        OptResult {
[2352](#2352)            changed: modified > 0,
[2353](#2353)            removed_count: 0,
[2354](#2354)            added_count: 0,
[2355](#2355)            modified_count: modified,
[2356](#2356)        }
[2357](#2357)    }
[2358](#2358)}
[2359](#2359)
[2360](#2360)impl Default for StrengthReduction {
[2361](#2361)    fn default() -> Self {
[2362](#2362)        Self::new()
[2363](#2363)    }
[2364](#2364)}

[2369](#2369)    }
[2370](#2370)
[2371](#2371)    fn run(&mut self, _cfg: &mut Cfg, instructions: &mut Vec<Instruction>) -> OptResult {
[2372](#2372)        self.reduce(instructions)
[2373](#2373)    }
[2374](#2374)}
[2375](#2375)
[2376](#2376)pub struct LoopInvariantCodeMotion {
[2378](#2378)    verbose: bool,
[2379](#2379)}
[2380](#2380)
[2381](#2381)impl LoopInvariantCodeMotion {
[2382](#2382)    pub fn new() -> Self {
[2383](#2383)        Self { verbose: false }
[2384](#2384)    }
[2385](#2385)
[2386](#2386)    pub fn with_verbose(mut self) -> Self {
[2387](#2387)        self.verbose = true;
[2388](#2388)        self
[2389](#2389)    }
[2390](#2390)
[2391](#2391)    fn detect_invariants(&self, cfg: &Cfg, instructions: &[Instruction]) -> HashSet<usize> {
[2393](#2393)        let mut invariants = HashSet::new();
[2394](#2394)
[2395](#2395)        for loop_info in &cfg.loops {
[2397](#2397)            for inst in instructions {
[2399](#2399)                if inst.is_dead || !loop_info.body.contains(&inst.block_id) {
[2400](#2400)                    continue;
[2401](#2401)                }
[2402](#2402)
[2403](#2403)                let is_invariant = match &inst.opcode {
[2405](#2405)                    Opcode::Const { .. } => true,
[2407](#2407)
[2408](#2408)                    Opcode::Add {
[2410](#2410)                        src1: _, src2: _, ..
[2411](#2411)                    }
[2412](#2412)                    | Opcode::Sub {
[2413](#2413)                        src1: _, src2: _, ..
[2414](#2414)                    }
[2415](#2415)                    | Opcode::Mul {
[2416](#2416)                        src1: _, src2: _, ..
[2417](#2417)                    } => {
[2418](#2418)                        false }
[2422](#2422)
[2423](#2423)                    Opcode::Load { .. } => false,
[2425](#2425)
[2426](#2426)                    _ => false,
[2427](#2427)                };
[2428](#2428)
[2429](#2429)                if is_invariant {
[2430](#2430)                    invariants.insert(inst.id);
[2431](#2431)                }
[2432](#2432)            }
[2433](#2433)        }
[2434](#2434)
[2435](#2435)        invariants
[2436](#2436)    }
[2437](#2437)
[2438](#2438)    fn hoist(&mut self, cfg: &mut Cfg, instructions: &mut [Instruction]) -> OptResult {
[2440](#2440)        let invariants = self.detect_invariants(cfg, instructions);
[2441](#2441)
[2442](#2442)        if self.verbose && !invariants.is_empty() {
[2445](#2445)            eprintln!(
[2446](#2446)                "LICM: {} loop-invariant instructions detected",
[2447](#2447)                invariants.len()
[2448](#2448)            );
[2449](#2449)        }
[2450](#2450)
[2451](#2451)        let modified = invariants.len();
[2452](#2452)
[2453](#2453)        OptResult {
[2454](#2454)            changed: modified > 0,
[2455](#2455)            removed_count: 0,
[2456](#2456)            added_count: 0,
[2457](#2457)            modified_count: modified,
[2458](#2458)        }
[2459](#2459)    }
[2460](#2460)}
[2461](#2461)
[2462](#2462)impl Default for LoopInvariantCodeMotion {
[2463](#2463)    fn default() -> Self {
[2464](#2464)        Self::new()
[2465](#2465)    }
[2466](#2466)}
[2467](#2467)
[2468](#2468)impl OptimizationPass for LoopInvariantCodeMotion {
[2469](#2469)    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
[2470](#2470)        "loop-invariant-code-motion"
[2471](#2471)    }
[2472](#2472)
[2473](#2473)    fn run(&mut self, cfg: &mut Cfg, instructions: &mut Vec<Instruction>) -> OptResult {
[2474](#2474)        self.hoist(cfg, instructions)
[2475](#2475)    }

[2478](#2478)pub struct CopyPropagation {
[2480](#2480)    verbose: bool,
[2481](#2481)}
[2482](#2482)
[2483](#2483)impl CopyPropagation {
[2484](#2484)    pub fn new() -> Self {
[2485](#2485)        Self { verbose: false }
[2486](#2486)    }
[2487](#2487)
[2488](#2488)    pub fn with_verbose(mut self) -> Self {
[2489](#2489)        self.verbose = true;
[2490](#2490)        self
[2491](#2491)    }
[2492](#2492)
[2493](#2493)    fn propagate(&mut self, instructions: &mut [Instruction]) -> OptResult {
[2495](#2495)        let copy_map: HashMap<Reg, Reg> = HashMap::new();
[2496](#2496)        let mut modified = 0;
[2497](#2497)
[2498](#2498)        for inst in instructions.iter_mut() {
[2505](#2505)            if inst.is_dead {
[2506](#2506)                continue;
[2507](#2507)            }
[2508](#2508)
[2509](#2509)            let mut changed = false;
[2510](#2510)            let opcode = inst.opcode.clone();
[2511](#2511)
[2512](#2512)            match opcode {
[2513](#2513)                Opcode::Add { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[2514](#2514)                    let new_src1 = Self::resolve(©_map, src1);
[2515](#2515)                    let new_src2 = Self::resolve(©_map, src2);
[2516](#2516)
[2517](#2517)                    if new_src1 != src1 || new_src2 != src2 {
[2518](#2518)                        inst.opcode = Opcode::Add {
[2519](#2519)                            dest,
[2520](#2520)                            src1: new_src1,
[2521](#2521)                            src2: new_src2,
[2522](#2522)                        };
[2523](#2523)                        changed = true;
[2524](#2524)                        modified += 1;
[2525](#2525)                    }
[2526](#2526)                }
[2527](#2527)
[2528](#2528)                Opcode::Sub { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[2529](#2529)                    let new_src1 = Self::resolve(©_map, src1);
[2530](#2530)                    let new_src2 = Self::resolve(©_map, src2);
[2531](#2531)
[2532](#2532)                    if new_src1 != src1 || new_src2 != src2 {
[2533](#2533)                        inst.opcode = Opcode::Sub {
[2534](#2534)                            dest,
[2535](#2535)                            src1: new_src1,
[2536](#2536)                            src2: new_src2,
[2537](#2537)                        };
[2538](#2538)                        changed = true;
[2539](#2539)                        modified += 1;
[2540](#2540)                    }
[2541](#2541)                }
[2542](#2542)
[2543](#2543)                Opcode::Mul { dest, src1, src2 } => {
[2544](#2544)                    let new_src1 = Self::resolve(©_map, src1);
[2545](#2545)                    let new_src2 = Self::resolve(©_map, src2);
[2546](#2546)
[2547](#2547)                    if new_src1 != src1 || new_src2 != src2 {
[2548](#2548)                        inst.opcode = Opcode::Mul {
[2549](#2549)                            dest,
[2550](#2550)                            src1: new_src1,
[2551](#2551)                            src2: new_src2,
[2552](#2552)                        };
[2553](#2553)                        changed = true;
[2554](#2554)                        modified += 1;
[2555](#2555)                    }
[2556](#2556)                }
[2557](#2557)
[2558](#2558)                Opcode::Load { dest: _, addr: _ } => {
[2559](#2559)                    }
[2561](#2561)
[2562](#2562)                Opcode::Store { src, addr } => {
[2563](#2563)                    let new_src = Self::resolve(©_map, src);
[2564](#2564)
[2565](#2565)                    if new_src != src {
[2566](#2566)                        inst.opcode = Opcode::Store { src: new_src, addr };
[2567](#2567)                        changed = true;
[2568](#2568)                        modified += 1;
[2569](#2569)                    }
[2570](#2570)                }
[2571](#2571)
[2572](#2572)                _ => {}
[2573](#2573)            }
[2574](#2574)
[2575](#2575)            if changed && self.verbose {
[2576](#2576)                eprintln!("Copy propagation: updated instruction {}", inst.id);
[2577](#2577)            }
[2578](#2578)        }
[2579](#2579)
[2580](#2580)        if self.verbose && modified > 0 {
[2581](#2581)            eprintln!("Copy propagation: {} instructions updated", modified);
[2582](#2582)        }
[2583](#2583)
[2584](#2584)        OptResult {
[2585](#2585)            changed: modified > 0,
[2586](#2586)            removed_count: 0,
[2587](#2587)            added_count: 0,
[2588](#2588)            modified_count: modified,
[2589](#2589)        }
[2590](#2590)    }
[2591](#2591)
[2592](#2592)    fn resolve(copy_map: &HashMap<Reg, Reg>, reg: Reg) -> Reg {
[2594](#2594)        let mut current = reg;
[2595](#2595)        let mut visited = HashSet::new();
[2596](#2596)
[2597](#2597)        while let Some(&next) = copy_map.get(¤t) {
[2599](#2599)            if !visited.insert(current) {
[2600](#2600)                break;
[2602](#2602)            }
[2603](#2603)            if next == current {
[2604](#2604)                break;
[2606](#2606)            }
[2607](#2607)            current = next;
[2608](#2608)        }
[2609](#2609)
[2610](#2610)        current
[2611](#2611)    }
[2612](#2612)}
[2613](#2613)
[2614](#2614)impl Default for CopyPropagation {
[2615](#2615)    fn default() -> Self {
[2616](#2616)        Self::new()
[2617](#2617)    }

[2620](#2620)impl OptimizationPass for CopyPropagation {
[2621](#2621)    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
[2622](#2622)        "copy-propagation"
[2623](#2623)    }
[2624](#2624)
[2625](#2625)    fn run(&mut self, _cfg: &mut Cfg, instructions: &mut Vec<Instruction>) -> OptResult {
[2626](#2626)        self.propagate(instructions)

[2629](#2629)
[2630](#2630)pub struct InstructionCombining {
[2632](#2632)    verbose: bool,
[2633](#2633)}
[2634](#2634)
[2635](#2635)impl InstructionCombining {
[2636](#2636)    pub fn new() -> Self {
[2637](#2637)        Self { verbose: false }
[2638](#2638)    }
[2639](#2639)
[2640](#2640)    pub fn with_verbose(mut self) -> Self {
[2641](#2641)        self.verbose = true;
[2642](#2642)        self
[2643](#2643)    }
[2644](#2644)
[2645](#2645)    fn combine(&mut self, instructions: &mut [Instruction]) -> OptResult {
[2647](#2647)        let mut const_values: HashMap<Reg, i32> = HashMap::new();
[2648](#2648)        let mut def_map: HashMap<Reg, usize> = HashMap::new();
[2649](#2649)        let mut inst_opcodes: HashMap<usize, Opcode> = HashMap::new();
[2650](#2650)        let mut modified = 0;
[2651](#2651)
[2652](#2652)        for inst in instructions.iter() {
[2654](#2654)            if inst.is_dead {
[2655](#2655)                continue;
[2656](#2656)            }
[2657](#2657)
[2658](#2658)            match &inst.opcode {
[2659](#2659)                Opcode::Const { dest, value } => {
[2660](#2660)                    const_values.insert(*dest, *value);
[2661](#2661)                    def_map.insert(*dest, inst.id);
[2662](#2662)                }
[2663](#2663)                Opcode::Add { dest, .. } | Opcode::Sub { dest, .. } | Opcode::Mul { dest, .. } => {
[2664](#2664)                    def_map.insert(*dest, inst.id);
[2665](#2665)                }
[2666](#2666)                _ => {}
[2667](#2667)            }
[2668](#2668)            inst_opcodes.insert(inst.id, inst.opcode.clone());
[2669](#2669)        }
[2670](#2670)
[2671](#2671)        for inst in instructions.iter() {
[2673](#2673)            if inst.is_dead {
[2674](#2674)                continue;
[2675](#2675)            }
[2676](#2676)
[2677](#2677)            match &inst.opcode {
[2678](#2678)                Opcode::Add {
[2680](#2680)                    dest: _,
[2681](#2681)                    src1,
[2682](#2682)                    src2,
[2683](#2683)                } => {
[2684](#2684)                    if let Some(&val2) = const_values.get(src2)
[2686](#2686)                        && let Some(&def_id) = def_map.get(src1)
[2687](#2687)                        && let Some(Opcode::Add {
[2688](#2688)                            dest: _,
[2689](#2689)                            src1: inner_src1,
[2690](#2690)                            src2: inner_src2,
[2691](#2691)                        }) = inst_opcodes.get(&def_id)
[2692](#2692)                        && let Some(&val1) = const_values.get(inner_src2)
[2693](#2693)                    {
[2694](#2694)                        let combined = val1.wrapping_add(val2);
[2696](#2696)
[2697](#2697)                        modified += 1;
[2700](#2700)
[2701](#2701)                        if self.verbose {
[2702](#2702)                            eprintln!(
[2703](#2703)                                "Instruction combining: (r{} + {}) + {} => r{} + {}",
[2704](#2704)                                inner_src1.0, val1, val2, inner_src1.0, combined
[2705](#2705)                            );
[2706](#2706)                        }
[2707](#2707)                    }
[2708](#2708)                }
[2709](#2709)
[2710](#2710)                Opcode::Mul {
[2714](#2714)                    dest: _,
[2715](#2715)                    src1: _,
[2716](#2716)                    src2: _,
[2717](#2717)                } => {
[2718](#2718)                    }
[2721](#2721)
[2722](#2722)                _ => {}
[2723](#2723)            }
[2724](#2724)        }
[2725](#2725)
[2726](#2726)        if self.verbose && modified > 0 {
[2727](#2727)            eprintln!("Instruction combining: {} opportunities found", modified);
[2728](#2728)        }
[2729](#2729)
[2730](#2730)        OptResult {
[2731](#2731)            changed: modified > 0,
[2732](#2732)            removed_count: 0,
[2733](#2733)            added_count: 0,
[2734](#2734)            modified_count: modified,
[2735](#2735)        }
[2736](#2736)    }
[2737](#2737)}
[2738](#2738)
[2739](#2739)impl Default for InstructionCombining {
[2740](#2740)    fn default() -> Self {
[2741](#2741)        Self::new()
[2742](#2742)    }
[2743](#2743)}
[2744](#2744)
[2745](#2745)impl OptimizationPass for InstructionCombining {
[2746](#2746)    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
[2747](#2747)        "instruction-combining"
[2748](#2748)    }
[2749](#2749)
[2750](#2750)    fn run(&mut self, _cfg: &mut Cfg, instructions: &mut Vec<Instruction>) -> OptResult {
[2751](#2751)        self.combine(instructions)
[2752](#2752)    }
[2753](#2753)}
[2754](#2754)
[2755](#2755)pub struct PassManager {
[2757](#2757)    passes: Vec<Box<dyn OptimizationPass>>,
[2758](#2758)    max_iterations: usize,
[2759](#2759)}
[2760](#2760)
[2761](#2761)impl PassManager {
[2762](#2762)    pub fn new() -> Self {
[2763](#2763)        Self {
[2764](#2764)            passes: Vec::new(),
[2765](#2765)            max_iterations: 10,
[2766](#2766)        }
[2767](#2767)    }
[2768](#2768)
[2769](#2769)    pub fn add_pass<P: OptimizationPass + 'static>(mut self, pass: P) -> Self {
[2770](#2770)        self.passes.push(Box::new(pass));
[2771](#2771)        self
[2772](#2772)    }
[2773](#2773)
[2774](#2774)    pub fn with_max_iterations(mut self, max: usize) -> Self {
[2775](#2775)        self.max_iterations = max;
[2776](#2776)        self
[2777](#2777)    }
[2778](#2778)
[2779](#2779)    pub fn run(&mut self, cfg: &mut Cfg, instructions: &mut Vec<Instruction>) -> OptResult {
[2780](#2780)        let mut total_result = OptResult::no_change();
[2781](#2781)        let mut iteration = 0;
[2782](#2782)
[2783](#2783)        loop {
[2784](#2784)            iteration += 1;
[2785](#2785)            if iteration > self.max_iterations {
[2786](#2786)                break;
[2787](#2787)            }
[2788](#2788)
[2789](#2789)            let mut iteration_result = OptResult::no_change();
[2790](#2790)
[2791](#2791)            for pass in &mut self.passes {
[2792](#2792)                let result = pass.run(cfg, instructions);
[2793](#2793)                iteration_result.merge(result);
[2794](#2794)            }
[2795](#2795)
[2796](#2796)            total_result.merge(iteration_result.clone());
[2797](#2797)
[2798](#2798)            if !iteration_result.changed {
[2800](#2800)                break;
[2801](#2801)            }
[2802](#2802)        }
[2803](#2803)
[2804](#2804)        total_result
[2805](#2805)    }
[2806](#2806)}
[2807](#2807)
[2808](#2808)impl Default for PassManager {
[2809](#2809)    fn default() -> Self {
[2810](#2810)        Self::new()
[2811](#2811)    }
[2812](#2812)}

[2937](#2937)    #[test]
[2938](#2938)    fn test_opt_result_merge() {
[2939](#2939)        let mut result1 = OptResult {
[2940](#2940)            changed: true,
[2941](#2941)            removed_count: 5,
[2942](#2942)            added_count: 2,
[2943](#2943)            modified_count: 3,
[2944](#2944)        };
[2945](#2945)
[2946](#2946)        let result2 = OptResult {
[2947](#2947)            changed: false,
[2948](#2948)            removed_count: 1,
[2949](#2949)            added_count: 1,
[2950](#2950)            modified_count: 2,
[2951](#2951)        };
[2952](#2952)
[2953](#2953)        result1.merge(result2);
[2954](#2954)
[2955](#2955)        assert!(result1.changed);
[2956](#2956)        assert_eq!(result1.removed_count, 6);
[2957](#2957)        assert_eq!(result1.added_count, 3);

[3873](#3873)                    dest: Reg(4),

[3895](#3895)            .add_pass(PeepholeOptimization::new())

[3916](#3916)

[3922](#3922)        }

[4085](#4085)    #[test]
[4086](#4086)    fn test_licm_detect_invariants() {
[4087](#4087)        let mut builder = CfgBuilder::new();
[4088](#4088)        let block0 = 0; let block1 = builder.start_block();
[4091](#4091)        let block2 = builder.start_block();
[4092](#4092)
[4093](#4093)        builder.set_current_block(block0);
[4095](#4095)        builder.add_branch(block1);
[4096](#4096)
[4097](#4097)        builder.set_current_block(block1);
[4098](#4098)        builder.add_branch(block2);
[4099](#4099)
[4100](#4100)        builder.set_current_block(block2);
[4101](#4101)        builder.add_branch(block1); builder.set_current_block(block1);
[4104](#4104)        builder.add_branch(block0); let mut cfg = builder.build();
[4107](#4107)
[4108](#4108)        cfg.loops.push(Loop {
[4110](#4110)            header: block1,
[4111](#4111)            body: vec![block1, block2].into_iter().collect(),
[4112](#4112)            depth: 1,
[4113](#4113)        });
[4114](#4114)
[4115](#4115)        let mut instructions = vec![
[4117](#4117)            Instruction {
[4119](#4119)                id: 0,
[4120](#4120)                opcode: Opcode::Const {
[4121](#4121)                    dest: Reg(0),
[4122](#4122)                    value: 10,
[4123](#4123)                },
[4124](#4124)                block_id: block1,
[4125](#4125)                is_dead: false,
[4126](#4126)            },
[4127](#4127)            Instruction {
[4129](#4129)                id: 1,
[4130](#4130)                opcode: Opcode::Add {
[4131](#4131)                    dest: Reg(2),
[4132](#4132)                    src1: Reg(1),
[4133](#4133)                    src2: Reg(0),
[4134](#4134)                },
[4135](#4135)                block_id: block1,
[4136](#4136)                is_dead: false,
[4137](#4137)            },
[4138](#4138)        ];
[4139](#4139)
[4140](#4140)        let mut licm = LoopInvariantCodeMotion::new();
[4141](#4141)        let result = licm.run(&mut cfg, &mut instructions);
[4142](#4142)
[4143](#4143)        assert!(result.changed);
[4145](#4145)        assert_eq!(result.modified_count, 1);
[4146](#4146)    }

### Load

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Store)

### Store

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.I64Load)

### I64Load

Load 64-bit value from local into register pair (for i64 on 32-bit ARM)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MemLoad)

### MemLoad

Load 32-bit value from linear memory: dest = mem[addr + offset]

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MemStore)

### MemStore

Store 32-bit value to linear memory: mem[addr + offset] = src

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MemLoadSubword)

### MemLoadSubword

Sub-word load: i32.load8_s/u, i32.load16_s/u and the i64 equivalents
after extension. `width` is 1 or 2 bytes; `signed` is true for the
`_s` variants. The dest is a single i32 register (sub-word loads on
ARM expand to a single LDRB/LDRH ± an SXTB/SXTH).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MemStoreSubword)

### MemStoreSubword

Sub-word store: i32.store8 / i32.store16 / i64.store8/16/32.
`width` is 1, 2, or 4. For 4-byte store of an i64’s low word we
just take the lo register.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.GlobalGet)

### GlobalGet

`global.get` — load a global into a fresh vreg. The actual ARM
lowering is `LDR rd, [R9, #offset]` (R9 is the globals base, by
convention). The vreg MUST be allocated to a non-AAPCS-param
register at lowering time — otherwise the LDR would clobber a
live caller arg.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.GlobalSet)

### GlobalSet

`global.set` — store a vreg to a global slot. Emits `STR src, [R9, #offset]`. No vreg is written.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MemorySize)

### MemorySize

`memory.size` — returns the current memory size in pages as an
i32. By convention R10 holds the memory-size word; we emit
`MOV dest, R10`. `dest` must be allocated to a non-param scratch.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.MemoryGrow)

### MemoryGrow

`memory.grow` — pops the grow-by amount, pushes the previous
page count (or -1 on failure). Embedded targets generally have
fixed memory, so this is a stub returning -1 in `dest`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Branch)

### Branch

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CondBranch)

### CondBranch

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Call)

### Call

Direct function call. Lowered to `BL func_<func_idx>` (or to an import
dispatch for `func_idx < num_imports`). The AAPCS return value lands in
`R0`, so `ir_to_arm` binds `dest` to `R0` after the BL.

Prior to this opcode, `WasmOp::Call` fell through to `Opcode::Nop` in
`wasm_to_ir`, leaving the call result’s vreg unmapped. Any downstream
consumer (e.g., `i32.add` of two `call` results, as in the recursive
`fib` example) then triggered the PR #101 defensive panic — or, with
the silent R0 fallback, silently miscompiled. See the issue-#93 family
of bugs.

NOTE: this opcode does NOT model the call’s clobber of R0..R3 — that’s a separate (deeper) issue around correct AAPCS lowering of calls in the optimized path. This fix only closes the unmapped-vreg gap so the compiler stops panicking on lawful WASM modules.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Return)

### Return

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Label)

### Label

Label marker for branch targets (loop start, block end)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Copy)

### Copy

Copy a value (for local.tee semantics: store value and keep it on stack)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.TeeStore)

### TeeStore

TeeStore: Store to local AND keep value on stack (local.tee) Combines Store + Copy: stores src to local addr, dest gets same value

### I64Extend32S

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.I64ExtendI32U)

### I64ExtendI32U

i32 -> i64 zero-extension. `dest_lo` aliases `src` (same vreg by IR
convention — see `wasm_to_ir`); `dest_hi` is freshly allocated and
holds the constant 0. Lowering MUST move `src`’s ARM reg into a
non-AAPCS-param register before treating it as the i64 lo half — the
downstream `I64Shl/ShrU/ShrS` emitters use `rm_lo`/`rm_hi` as scratch
and clobber them, so we must not place a live param register there.
This was the proximate cause of issue #93 (memset infinite loop on
silicon) before this opcode existed and the bridge silently fell
through to `Opcode::Nop` + `R0`-fallback in `get_arm_reg`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.I64ExtendI32S)

### I64ExtendI32S

i32 -> i64 sign-extension. Same constraints as I64ExtendI32U; the
`dest_hi` is filled by an arithmetic shift right by 31 of the src.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.I32WrapI64)

### I32WrapI64

i64 -> i32 wrap (truncate to low 32 bits). `dest` aliases the i64’s
`src_lo` vreg (same value); the high half is simply discarded.

# prost - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/prost/^0.13/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#prost)*PROST!*

`prost` is a [Protocol Buffers](https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/)
implementation for the [Rust Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/). `prost`
generates simple, idiomatic Rust code from `proto2` and `proto3` files.

Compared to other Protocol Buffers implementations, `prost`

- Generates simple, idiomatic, and readable Rust types by taking advantage of
Rust `derive`attributes.
- Retains comments from `.proto`files in generated Rust code.
- Allows existing Rust types (not generated from a `.proto`) to be serialized and deserialized by adding attributes.
- Uses the `bytes::{Buf, BufMut}``std::io::{Read, Write}`.
- Respects the Protobuf `package`specifier when organizing generated code into Rust modules.
- Preserves unknown enum values during deserialization.
- Does not include support for runtime reflection or message descriptors.

[§](https://docs.rs#using-prost-in-a-cargo-project)Using `prost` in a Cargo Project

First, add `prost` and its public dependencies to your `Cargo.toml`:

The recommended way to add `.proto` compilation to a Cargo project is to use the
`prost-build` library. See the [ prost-build documentation](https://docs.rs/prost-build/latest/prost_build/) for
more details and examples.

See the [snazzy repository](https://github.com/danburkert/snazzy) for a simple start-to-finish example.

[§](https://docs.rs#msrv)MSRV

`prost` follows the `tokio-rs` project’s MSRV model and supports 1.70. For more
information on the tokio msrv policy you can check it out [here](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/#supported-rust-versions)

[§](https://docs.rs#generated-code)Generated Code

`prost` generates Rust code from source `.proto` files using the `proto2` or
`proto3` syntax. `prost`’s goal is to make the generated code as simple as
possible.

[§](https://docs.rs#protoc)`protoc`

With `prost-build` v0.11 release, `protoc` will be required to invoke
`compile_protos` (unless `skip_protoc` is enabled). Prost will no longer provide
bundled `protoc` or attempt to compile `protoc` for users. For install
instructions for `protoc`, please check out the [protobuf install](https://github.com/protocolbuffers/protobuf#protobuf-compiler-installation) instructions.

[§](https://docs.rs#packages)Packages

Prost can now generate code for `.proto` files that don’t have a package spec.
`prost` will translate the Protobuf package into
a Rust module. For example, given the `package` specifier:

`package foo.bar;`All Rust types generated from the file will be in the `foo::bar` module.

[§](https://docs.rs#messages)Messages

Given a simple message declaration:

```
// Sample message.
message Foo {
}
```
`prost` will generate the following Rust struct:

[§](https://docs.rs#fields-1)Fields

Fields in Protobuf messages are translated into Rust as public struct fields of the corresponding type.

[§](https://docs.rs#scalar-values)Scalar Values

Scalar value types are converted as follows:

| Protobuf Type | Rust Type |
|---|---|
| `double` | `f64` |
| `float` | `f32` |
| `int32` | `i32` |
| `int64` | `i64` |
| `uint32` | `u32` |
| `uint64` | `u64` |
| `sint32` | `i32` |
| `sint64` | `i64` |
| `fixed32` | `u32` |
| `fixed64` | `u64` |
| `sfixed32` | `i32` |
| `sfixed64` | `i64` |
| `bool` | `bool` |
| `string` | `String` |
| `bytes` | `Vec<u8>` |

[§](https://docs.rs#enumerations)Enumerations

All `.proto` enumeration types convert to the Rust `i32` type. Additionally,
each enumeration type gets a corresponding Rust `enum` type. For example, this
`proto` enum:

```
enum PhoneType {
  MOBILE = 0;
  HOME = 1;
  WORK = 2;
}
```
gets this corresponding Rust enum  1:

You can convert a `PhoneType` value to an `i32` by doing:

The `#[derive(::prost::Enumeration)]` annotation added to the generated
`PhoneType` adds these associated functions to the type:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
impl PhoneType {
    pub fn is_valid(value: i32) -> bool { ... }
    #[deprecated]
    pub fn from_i32(value: i32) -> Option<PhoneType> { ... }
}
```
It also adds an `impl TryFrom<i32> for PhoneType`, so you can convert an `i32` to its corresponding `PhoneType` value by doing,
for example:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
let phone_type = 2i32;
match PhoneType::try_from(phone_type) {
    Ok(PhoneType::Mobile) => ...,
    Ok(PhoneType::Home) => ...,
    Ok(PhoneType::Work) => ...,
    Err(_) => ...,
}
```
Additionally, wherever a `proto` enum is used as a field in a `Message`, the
message will have ‘accessor’ methods to get/set the value of the field as the
Rust enum type. For instance, this proto `PhoneNumber` message that has a field
named `type` of type `PhoneType`:

```
message PhoneNumber {
  string number = 1;
  PhoneType type = 2;
}
```
will become the following Rust type  2 with methods

`type` and `set_type`:[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
pub struct PhoneNumber {
    pub number: String,
    pub r#type: i32, // the `r#` is needed because `type` is a Rust keyword
}
impl PhoneNumber {
    pub fn r#type(&self) -> PhoneType { ... }
    pub fn set_type(&mut self, value: PhoneType) { ... }
}
```
Note that the getter methods will return the Rust enum’s default value if the
field has an invalid `i32` value.

The `enum` type isn’t used directly as a field, because the Protobuf spec
mandates that enumerations values are ‘open’, and decoding unrecognized
enumeration values must be possible.

[§](https://docs.rs#field-modifiers)Field Modifiers

Protobuf scalar value and enumeration message fields can have a modifier depending on the Protobuf version. Modifiers change the corresponding type of the Rust field:

| `.proto`Version | Modifier | Rust Type |
|---|---|---|
| `proto2` | `optional` | `Option<T>` |
| `proto2` | `required` | `T` |
| `proto3` | default | `T`for scalar types,`Option<T>`otherwise |
| `proto3` | `optional` | `Option<T>` |
| `proto2`/`proto3` | `repeated` | `Vec<T>` |

Note that in `proto3` the default representation for all user-defined message
types is `Option<T>`, and for scalar types just `T` (during decoding, a missing
value is populated by `T::default()`). If you need a witness of the presence of
a scalar type `T`, use the `optional` modifier to enforce an `Option<T>`
representation in the generated Rust struct.

[§](https://docs.rs#map-fields)Map Fields

Map fields are converted to a Rust `HashMap` with key and value type converted
from the Protobuf key and value types.

[§](https://docs.rs#message-fields)Message Fields

Message fields are converted to the corresponding struct type. The table of
field modifiers above applies to message fields, except that `proto3` message
fields without a modifier (the default) will be wrapped in an `Option`.
Typically message fields are unboxed. `prost` will automatically box a message
field if the field type and the parent type are recursively nested in order to
avoid an infinite sized struct.

[§](https://docs.rs#oneof-fields)Oneof Fields

Oneof fields convert to a Rust enum. Protobuf `oneof`s types are not named, so
`prost` uses the name of the `oneof` field for the resulting Rust enum, and
defines the enum in a module under the struct. For example, a `proto3` message
such as:

```
message Foo {
  oneof widget {
    int32 quux = 1;
    string bar = 2;
  }
}
```
generates the following Rust 3:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
pub struct Foo {
    pub widget: Option<foo::Widget>,
}
pub mod foo {
    pub enum Widget {
        Quux(i32),
        Bar(String),
    }
}
```
`oneof` fields are always wrapped in an `Option`.

[§](https://docs.rs#services)Services

`prost-build` allows a custom code-generator to be used for processing `service`
definitions. This can be used to output Rust traits according to an
application’s specific needs.

[§](https://docs.rs#generated-code-example)Generated Code Example

Example `.proto` file:

```
syntax = "proto3";
package tutorial;
message Person {
  string name = 1;
  int32 id = 2;  // Unique ID number for this person.
  string email = 3;
  enum PhoneType {
    MOBILE = 0;
    HOME = 1;
    WORK = 2;
  }
  message PhoneNumber {
    string number = 1;
    PhoneType type = 2;
  }
  repeated PhoneNumber phones = 4;
}
// Our address book file is just one of these.
message AddressBook {
  repeated Person people = 1;
}
```
and the generated Rust code (`tutorial.rs`):

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, ::prost::Message)]
pub struct Person {
    #[prost(string, tag="1")]
    pub name: ::prost::alloc::string::String,
    /// Unique ID number for this person.
    #[prost(int32, tag="2")]
    pub id: i32,
    #[prost(string, tag="3")]
    pub email: ::prost::alloc::string::String,
    #[prost(message, repeated, tag="4")]
    pub phones: ::prost::alloc::vec::Vec<person::PhoneNumber>,
}
/// Nested message and enum types in `Person`.
pub mod person {
    #[derive(Clone, PartialEq, ::prost::Message)]
    pub struct PhoneNumber {
        #[prost(string, tag="1")]
        pub number: ::prost::alloc::string::String,
        #[prost(enumeration="PhoneType", tag="2")]
        pub r#type: i32,
    }
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, ::prost::Enumeration)]
    #[repr(i32)]
    pub enum PhoneType {
        Mobile = 0,
        Home = 1,
        Work = 2,
    }
}
/// Our address book file is just one of these.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, ::prost::Message)]
pub struct AddressBook {
    #[prost(message, repeated, tag="1")]
    pub people: ::prost::alloc::vec::Vec<Person>,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#accessing-the-protoc-filedescriptorset)Accessing the `protoc` `FileDescriptorSet`

The `prost_build::Config::file_descriptor_set_path` option can be used to emit a file descriptor set
during the build & code generation step. When used in conjunction with the `std::include_bytes`
macro and the `prost_types::FileDescriptorSet` type, applications and libraries using Prost can
implement introspection capabilities requiring details from the original `.proto` files.

[§](https://docs.rs#using-prost-in-a-no_std-crate)Using `prost` in a `no_std` Crate

`prost` is compatible with `no_std` crates. To enable `no_std` support, disable
the `std` features in `prost` and `prost-types`:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
[dependencies]
prost = { version = "0.13.5", default-features = false, features = ["prost-derive"] }
prost-types = { version = "0.13.5", default-features = false }
```
Additionally, configure `prost-build` to output `BTreeMap`s instead of `HashMap`s
for all Protobuf `map` fields in your `build.rs`:

When using edition 2015, it may be necessary to add an `extern crate core;`
directive to the crate which includes `prost`-generated code.

[§](https://docs.rs#serializing-existing-types)Serializing Existing Types

`prost` uses a custom derive macro to handle encoding and decoding types, which
means that if your existing Rust type is compatible with Protobuf types, you can
serialize and deserialize it by adding the appropriate derive and field
annotations.

Currently the best documentation on adding annotations is to look at the generated code examples above.

[§](https://docs.rs#tag-inference-for-existing-types)Tag Inference for Existing Types

Prost automatically infers tags for the struct.

Fields are tagged sequentially in the order they
are specified, starting with `1`.

You may skip tags which have been reserved, or where there are gaps between
sequentially occurring tag values by specifying the tag number to skip to with
the `tag` attribute on the first field after the gap. The following fields will
be tagged sequentially starting from the next number.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use prost;
use prost::{Enumeration, Message};
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Message)]
struct Person {
    #[prost(string, tag = "1")]
    pub id: String, // tag=1
    // NOTE: Old "name" field has been removed
    // pub name: String, // tag=2 (Removed)
    #[prost(string, tag = "6")]
    pub given_name: String, // tag=6
    #[prost(string)]
    pub family_name: String, // tag=7
    #[prost(string)]
    pub formatted_name: String, // tag=8
    #[prost(uint32, tag = "3")]
    pub age: u32, // tag=3
    #[prost(uint32)]
    pub height: u32, // tag=4
    #[prost(enumeration = "Gender")]
    pub gender: i32, // tag=5
    // NOTE: Skip to less commonly occurring fields
    #[prost(string, tag = "16")]
    pub name_prefix: String, // tag=16  (eg. mr/mrs/ms)
    #[prost(string)]
    pub name_suffix: String, // tag=17  (eg. jr/esq)
    #[prost(string)]
    pub maiden_name: String, // tag=18
}
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Enumeration)]
pub enum Gender {
    Unknown = 0,
    Female = 1,
    Male = 2,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#nix)Nix

The prost project maintains flakes support for local development. Once you have
nix and nix flakes setup you can just run `nix develop` to get a shell
configured with the required dependencies to compile the whole project.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

- `std`: Enable integration with standard library. Disable this feature for- `no_std`support. This feature is enabled by default.
- `derive`: Enable integration with- `prost-derive`. Disable this feature to reduce compile times. This feature is enabled by default.
- `prost-derive`: Deprecated. Alias for- `derive`feature.
- `no-recursion-limit`: Disable the recursion limit. The recursion limit is 100 and cannot be customized.

[§](https://docs.rs#faq)FAQ

- **Could**- `prost`be implemented as a serializer for- [Serde](https://serde.rs/)?

Probably not, however I would like to hear from a Serde expert on the matter. There are two complications with trying to serialize Protobuf messages with Serde:

- Protobuf fields require a numbered tag, and currently there appears to be no
mechanism suitable for this in `serde`.
- The mapping of Protobuf type to Rust type is not 1-to-1. As a result,
trait-based approaches to dispatching don’t work very well. Example: six
different Protobuf field types correspond to a Rust `Vec<i32>`:`repeated int32`,`repeated sint32`,`repeated sfixed32`, and their packed counterparts.

But it is possible to place `serde` derive tags onto the generated types, so
the same structure can support both `prost` and `Serde`.

- **I get errors when trying to run**- `cargo test`on MacOS

If the errors are about missing `autoreconf` or similar, you can probably fix
them by running

# prost_types - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/prost-types/^0.13/

## Expand description

Protocol Buffers well-known types.

Note that the documentation for the types defined in this crate are generated from the Protobuf definitions, so code examples are not in Rust.

See the [Protobuf reference](https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/google.protobuf) for more information about well-known types.

[§](https://docs.rs#any)Any

The well-known [ Any](https://docs.rs/struct.Any.html) type contains an arbitrary serialized message along with a URL that
describes the type of the serialized message. Every message that also implements

[can be serialized to and deserialized from](https://docs.rs/prost/0.13.5/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/prost/name/trait.Name.html)

`Name`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Any.html)

`Any`[§](https://docs.rs#serialization)Serialization

A message can be serialized using [ Any::from_msg](https://docs.rs/struct.Any.html#method.from_msg).

```
let message = Timestamp::date(2000, 1, 1).unwrap();
let any = Any::from_msg(&message).unwrap();
```
[§](https://docs.rs#deserialization)Deserialization

A message can be deserialized using [ Any::to_msg](https://docs.rs/struct.Any.html#method.to_msg).

`let message = any.to_msg::<Timestamp>().unwrap();`[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature Flags

- `std`: Enable integration with standard library. Disable this feature for- `no_std`support. This feature is enabled by default.
- `arbitrary`: Enable integration with crate- `arbitrary`. All types on this crate will implement- `trait Arbitrary`.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Any](https://docs.rs/struct.Any.html)
- `Any`contains an arbitrary serialized protocol buffer message along with a URL that describes the type of the serialized message.
- [Api](https://docs.rs/struct.Api.html)
- Api is a light-weight descriptor for an API Interface.
- [Descriptor](https://docs.rs/struct.DescriptorProto.html)- Proto
- Describes a message type.
- [Duration](https://docs.rs/struct.Duration.html)
- A Duration represents a signed, fixed-length span of time represented as a count of seconds and fractions of seconds at nanosecond resolution. It is independent of any calendar and concepts like “day” or “month”. It is related to Timestamp in that the difference between two Timestamp values is a Duration and it can be added or subtracted from a Timestamp. Range is approximately +-10,000 years.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/struct.Enum.html)
- Enum type definition.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/struct.EnumDescriptorProto.html)- Descriptor - Proto
- Describes an enum type.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/struct.EnumOptions.html)- Options
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/struct.EnumValue.html)- Value
- Enum value definition.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/struct.EnumValueDescriptorProto.html)- Value - Descriptor - Proto
- Describes a value within an enum.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/struct.EnumValueOptions.html)- Value - Options
- [Extension](https://docs.rs/struct.ExtensionRangeOptions.html)- Range - Options
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.Field.html)
- A single field of a message type.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldDescriptorProto.html)- Descriptor - Proto
- Describes a field within a message.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldMask.html)- Mask
- `FieldMask`represents a set of symbolic field paths, for example:
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldOptions.html)- Options
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileDescriptorProto.html)- Descriptor - Proto
- Describes a complete .proto file.
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileDescriptorSet.html)- Descriptor - Set
- The protocol compiler can output a FileDescriptorSet containing the .proto files it parses.
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.FileOptions.html)- Options
- Each of the definitions above may have “options” attached. These are just annotations which may cause code to be generated slightly differently or may contain hints for code that manipulates protocol messages.
- [Generated](https://docs.rs/struct.GeneratedCodeInfo.html)- Code - Info
- Describes the relationship between generated code and its original source file. A GeneratedCodeInfo message is associated with only one generated source file, but may contain references to different source .proto files.
- [List](https://docs.rs/struct.ListValue.html)- Value
- `ListValue`is a wrapper around a repeated field of values.
- [Message](https://docs.rs/struct.MessageOptions.html)- Options
- [Method](https://docs.rs/struct.Method.html)
- Method represents a method of an API interface.
- [Method](https://docs.rs/struct.MethodDescriptorProto.html)- Descriptor - Proto
- Describes a method of a service.
- [Method](https://docs.rs/struct.MethodOptions.html)- Options
- [Mixin](https://docs.rs/struct.Mixin.html)
- Declares an API Interface to be included in this interface. The including interface must redeclare all the methods from the included interface, but documentation and options are inherited as follows:
- [Oneof](https://docs.rs/struct.OneofDescriptorProto.html)- Descriptor - Proto
- Describes a oneof.
- [Oneof](https://docs.rs/struct.OneofOptions.html)- Options
- [Option](https://docs.rs/struct.Option.html)
- A protocol buffer option, which can be attached to a message, field, enumeration, etc.
- [Service](https://docs.rs/struct.ServiceDescriptorProto.html)- Descriptor - Proto
- Describes a service.
- [Service](https://docs.rs/struct.ServiceOptions.html)- Options
- [Source](https://docs.rs/struct.SourceCodeInfo.html)- Code - Info
- Encapsulates information about the original source file from which a FileDescriptorProto was generated.
- [Source](https://docs.rs/struct.SourceContext.html)- Context
- `SourceContext`represents information about the source of a protobuf element, like the file in which it is defined.
- [Struct](https://docs.rs/struct.Struct.html)
- `Struct`represents a structured data value, consisting of fields which map to dynamically typed values. In some languages,- `Struct`might be supported by a native representation. For example, in scripting languages like JS a struct is represented as an object. The details of that representation are described together with the proto support for the language.
- [Timestamp](https://docs.rs/struct.Timestamp.html)
- A Timestamp represents a point in time independent of any time zone or local calendar, encoded as a count of seconds and fractions of seconds at nanosecond resolution. The count is relative to an epoch at UTC midnight on January 1, 1970, in the proleptic Gregorian calendar which extends the Gregorian calendar backwards to year one.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.Type.html)
- A protocol buffer message type.
- [Uninterpreted](https://docs.rs/struct.UninterpretedOption.html)- Option
- A message representing a option the parser does not recognize. This only appears in options protos created by the compiler::Parser class. DescriptorPool resolves these when building Descriptor objects. Therefore, options protos in descriptor objects (e.g. returned by Descriptor::options(), or produced by Descriptor::CopyTo()) will never have UninterpretedOptions in them.
- [Value](https://docs.rs/struct.Value.html)
- `Value`represents a dynamically typed value which can be either null, a number, a string, a boolean, a recursive struct value, or a list of values. A producer of value is expected to set one of these variants. Absence of any variant indicates an error.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Duration](https://docs.rs/enum.DurationError.html)- Error
- A duration handling error.
- [Null](https://docs.rs/enum.NullValue.html)- Value
- `NullValue`is a singleton enumeration to represent the null value for the- `Value`type union.
- [Syntax](https://docs.rs/enum.Syntax.html)
- The syntax in which a protocol buffer element is defined.
- [Timestamp](https://docs.rs/enum.TimestampError.html)- Error
- A timestamp handling error.

# gravity_proto - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/gravity_proto/0.11.0/target-redirect/gravity_proto/

## Expand description

This crate provides Gravity proto definitions in Rust and also re-exports cosmos_sdk_proto for use by downstream crates. By default around a dozen proto files are generated and places into the prost folder. We could then proceed to fix up all these files and use them as the required dependencies to the Gravity file, but we chose instead to replace those paths with references ot upstream cosmos-sdk-proto and delete the other files. This reduces cruft in this repo even if it does make for a somewhat more confusing proto generation process.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [cosmos_sdk_proto](https://docs.rs/cosmos-sdk-proto-althea/0.20.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/cosmos_sdk_proto_althea/index.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [auction](https://docs.rs/auction/index.html)
- [gravity](https://docs.rs/gravity/index.html)
- [gravity_](https://docs.rs/gravity_test/index.html)- test
- note to future readers I have hand copied the RegisteredInterchainAccount file from ibc.applications.interchain_accounts.v1.rs which is compiled but not checked in into gaia.icaauth.v1.rs

---
